svg.text: 4WD AUTONOMOUS CAR — COMPLETE BREADBOARD-LESS WIRING SCHEMATIC
Phase 1 (Ultrasonic + 230° Servo) | Phase 2 (+ 2x IR Sensors) | Phase 3 (+ ESP32-CAM & ML Control) — All Powered via Buck Converter
Use Main Toggle Switch on (+) Wire
Twist/Splice wires or clamp in Screw Terminal Block (No Breadboard Needed!)
Remove ENA & ENB 5V Jumpers for PWM Speed Control
Timer1 used by Servo.h → Motor PWM kept on Timer0 (D5 & D6) so PWM never conflicts!
• U0T (GPIO1 TX) → Arduino Pin A2 (SoftSerial RX) [1 Direct Wire]
• IO13 (telemetry in) ← Optional: Uno A3 via 1kΩ/2kΩ divider
• Streams MJPEG Video over Wi-Fi → Python ML → Sends F/L/R/B/S to Uno
• Flash note: Jumper IO0-to-GND while uploading code, then remove IO0 jumper.
HOW TO CONNECT EVERYTHING CLEANLY WITHOUT A BREADBOARD (3 PROVEN METHODS)
METHOD A: USE SCREW TERMINALS + UNO ICSP PINS
1. L298N has screw terminals for +12V, GND, and +5V. Each screw
terminal easily clamps 3–4 stripped jumper wire ends together!
2. Arduino Uno has 3x GND pins on standard headers PLUS 1x 5V
and 1x GND male pin on the 6-pin ICSP header (near reset button).
→ Zero soldering & zero breadboard required for Phase 1 & 2!
METHOD B: MAKE A 5V & GND Y-SPLICE HARNESS
1. Take 6 Red (5V) jumper wires: cut one end off each, strip 1 cm
of insulation, twist all 6 copper cores together tightly, and
wrap with electrical tape (or clamp into Buck OUT+).
2. Repeat with 6 Black (GND) wires tied to Buck OUT- & Uno GND.
→ Vibration-proof! Never shakes loose on a moving 4WD chassis.
• All signal pins (IN1-IN4, ENA/B, TRIG, ECHO, SERVO, IR_L, IR_R,
• Plug Female end directly onto the sensor/module male header pin,
and plug the Male end directly into the Arduino Uno female socket.
→ Every signal pin has its own dedicated Arduino Uno header slot!
